info.title: Invinite API
info.description:
Invinite financial data API. Each endpoint has a base credit cost: `x-credits` is the base cost; responses add 1 credit per started 1,000 rows beyond the first 1,000; `X-Credits-Charged` reports the final debit and `X-Credits-Included-Remaining` what is left of the plan's included credits. `GET /v1/account/usage` returns your team's usage by day, endpoint family and key (it costs no credits). SEC filing search has a 100-credit base cost.

## Webhooks

PRO teams subscribe with `POST /v1/earnings-calls/webhooks` to the `earnings_call.*` lifecycle events (filtered by CIK); see `x-webhooks` for each `data` object. Every delivery is a `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Invinite-Event`, `X-Invinite-Delivery` and `X-Invinite-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` where `v1` = HMAC-SHA256(secret, `<t>.<raw body>`); during a secret rotation the header carries one `v1` per valid secret. Reject a signature older than 5 minutes. Any 2xx within 10 s acknowledges; redirects are not followed. A failed delivery is retried after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h, 24 h (8 attempts in all, the same delivery id each time). A subscription is disabled after 8 consecutive dead-lettered deliveries (a final `ping` with `notice: subscription_disabled` is sent). Deliveries are at-least-once and unordered: dedupe on the delivery id, order by `created_at`.

## Licensing

| Tier | display | redistribute | rag | train | audio | resell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FREE | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – |
| LITE | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – |
| STANDARD | ✓ | – | ✓ | – | – | – |
| PRO | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – | ✓ | – |

Invinite data may be shown and, from PRO, redistributed inside the licensee's own product with attribution ("Source: Invinite" on screen or in the API response that carries it). It may never be resold, relicensed, white-labelled or offered as a data feed as the licensee's own data, at any tier, under any contract.

Policy version: 2026-10-draft. Draft — pending counsel sign-off.

Audio files are forensically watermarked per customer. Audio is served through signed URLs, is subject to per-company takedown and may not be re-hosted; every delivered file carries a per-team forensic watermark (tasks 32 / 43 / 51): a copy found elsewhere is traced to the team that received it.

SEC data: Figures and filings originate from SEC EDGAR; the standardisation, mapping and derived metrics are Invinite's.

Every `/v1/*` data operation carries `x-license`, the minimum use right its data ships with; `GET /status/licensing` serves the same matrix per route. `/v1/account/usage` serves no licensed data and carries none.

## Status

[`/status`](/status) reports request health per product family, [`/status/earnings-calls`](/status/earnings-calls) the earnings-call pipeline and [`/status/licensing`](/status/licensing) the licensing matrix per route. The status routes need no API key and are cached for 5 minutes.

Measured inside the API process per product family and UTC day: availability = non-5xx responses / responses (admission 429 / 503 included), latency = time from request arrival to the response, excluding network and edge time; percentiles are bucket upper bounds (conservative), the current day is partial.

Product families: Company, Financials, SEC Filings, Insider Trades, Institutional Ownership, IPOs, Market, Metadata, Earnings Calls, WebSocket, Account.

Data freshness: the newest ingested record of each data set that carries an ingest timestamp (SEC filings, insider trades, institutional ownership, IPOs, earnings-call transcripts), each read with one indexed MAX() under a 2-second statement timeout; financial statements and market holidays have no ingest timestamp and are listed as `no_timestamp`, a data set the deployment does not measure as `not_measured`, a failed read as `unavailable`.

Earnings-call pipeline SLO targets: first live segment p95 ≤ 30 s after call start, final transcript p95 ≤ 300 s after call end; p95 is published per webcast vendor per day.

WebSocketNewFilingEvent.description: Broadcast when a new SEC filing finishes processing

WebSocketPingEvent.description: Server heartbeat payload sent when protocol-level ping is unavailable

WebSocketSubscribeEarningsCall.description: Client frame: subscribe to the live transcript of one earnings call, by event_id or by cik (the call that is live or starts within ±2 h), or with scope: all_live (no event_id / cik) to every call being captured live — keyword hits only, never segments, one subscription slot. Requires the PRO plan.

event_id.description: Event id from the earnings-calls REST routes

scope.description: all_live = every live call (keywords required, error keywords_required without); then no event_id / cik

since_seq.description: Last final seq the client holds; finals after it are replayed before live delivery (-1 = from the first final)

partials.description: Also receive partial (not yet final) segments

prices.description: Also receive price_tick frames of the call's stock (≤ 1 per second while the call is live). Per-call only: with scope: all_live the subscribe is refused (bad_message). GET /v1/earnings-calls/live says live_prices: true when ticks flow

keywords.description: Keyword alerts: a keyword_hit frame for every FINAL segment that contains one (whole words, case-insensitive, multi-word allowed). Held for this subscription only

keyword_match.description: exact = whole-word match of your spelling (buyback never matches buybacks); stem = also s / es / ed / ing / 's per word (tariff matches tariffs)

speaker_roles.description: Only hits spoken by one of these roles (from the provisional live speaker names; a hit whose speaker is still unnamed passes)

min_rank.description: all_live only: calls of companies ranked ≤ min_rank by market cap

events.description: all_live only: what reaches the subscription (default keyword_hit; add guidance_flash to receive the flashes of every live call)

WebSocketSubscribedEvent.description: A subscription is active. A per-call subscription carries the call (event_id … state); a scope: all_live subscription carries scope, keywords and live_calls instead

current_seq.description: Highest final seq seen so far; null before the first final (seqs start at 0)

keywords.description: all_live only: the keywords as held

live_calls.description: all_live only: calls being captured live that the subscription follows right now

WebSocketKeywordHitEvent.description: A subscribed keyword occurred in a FINAL segment (layer live; partials are never evaluated) or, once per subscription at transcript_ready, in the final transcript (layer final; a final hit within ± 5 s of a live hit of the same keyword is not repeated). The only call-level frame of a scope: all_live subscription besides guidance_flash

keyword.description: The subscriber's own spelling of the keyword

seq.description: The live final's seq; null on the final layer

start_ms.description: Offset from the start of the recording

end_ms.description: null on the final layer when the cleaned text has no end timing

text.description: The segment (live) or turn (final), at most 500 chars

context_before.description: The previous final / turn of the call (≤ 300 chars); a final is often half a sentence

speaker_name.description: From the live speaker-name snapshot (null while unnamed) or the final transcript

speaker_role.description: executive | ir_host | analyst | operator; null while unnamed

layer.description: live = a live final; final = the final transcript at transcript_ready (once per subscription)

latency_ms.description: live only: relay time inside the API process minus the segment's own end time (excludes the client's network); null when the call's clock is unknown

WebSocketGuidanceFlashEvent.description: A forward-looking guidance number extracted from the live transcript seconds after it was spoken (one frame per metric / period; a restatement repeats it with a higher revision). Sent to every subscription of the call and to all_live subscriptions whose events include guidance_flash. Provisional: the structured guidance of /v1/earnings-calls/extractions replaces it after the call

seq.description: The final that triggered the extraction

revision.description: 1 for the first flash of a metric / period; higher when the numbers were restated

low.description: Lower bound of the range (absolute units)

point.description: A point value when no range was given

source_sentence.description: The verbatim sentence the numbers come from

start_ms.description: Offset of the sentence from the start of the recording

WebSocketPriceTickEvent.description: One second of the call's stock price while the call is live (≤ 1 per second, only seconds with a trade — hold the last value and draw a missing second as a gap; pre-market and after-hours bars are sparse). Sent only to per-call subscriptions with prices: true. Temporal coincidence, not attribution of cause. The minute rows of /v1/earnings-calls/price-attribution are the backlog for a late join

at.description: Start of the one-second bar (ISO 8601 UTC)

call_ms.description: The bar start on the transcript clock (the start_ms of transcript_segment frames); null before the call's clock is known — then chart it on wall time (at)

price.description: Last price of the second, shown while the call is live

cumulative_volume.description: Shares traded so far today; null when unknown

reference_price.description: The call's reference: the last trade before the call start (for a late join, the previous close)

return_bps.description: Return since reference_price, basis points; null without a reference

day_return_bps.description: Return since prev_close, basis points; null without it

source.description: stream = the real-time per-second bar; snapshot = the polled last trade while the stream is down (open = high = low = price)

WebSocketWarningEvent.description: A subscription is degraded but keeps running: global_scope_degraded = a new live call was not attached because this server already follows its cap of live calls (sent once per subscription while the cap holds)

WebSocketTranscriptSegmentEvent.description: One live transcript segment. seq is strictly increasing per call but not contiguous; a partial carries the seq its final will get

start_ms.description: Offset from the start of the recording

WebSocketSpeakerNamesEvent.description: Provisional live speaker names (the newest snapshot; the final transcript's naming replaces them). A final's name = the assignment of its speaker_label whose seq range covers its seq

WebSocketCallLifecycleEvent.description: A phase of the call: call_started, call_ended, transcript_provisional, transcript_ready or rescheduled. transcript_ready and rescheduled end the subscription (an unsubscribed frame follows; after rescheduled, subscribe again with the same event_id)

live_transcript_available.description: call_ended only: the provisional live transcript is available (null = unknown)

WebSocketGapEvent.description: No final between after_seq and next_seq arrived within the reorder wait (a capture relaunch skips 1,000+ numbers with nothing lost, or finals were never published). A late final may still follow: order by seq

WebSocketUnsubscribedEvent.description: A subscription ended: on request, after transcript_ready / rescheduled, 2 h after call_ended without transcript_ready, when the call will produce nothing more (capture failed, no call, published), or 12 h after the scheduled start

reason.description: requested | transcript_ready | rescheduled | no_transcript (2 h after call_ended) | call_not_live (capture failed, no call, or published) | max_duration (12 h after the scheduled start)

WebSocketErrorEvent.description: A client frame was refused (unavailable = an unexpected server failure, retry shortly); the socket stays open

id.description: Delivery id (= X-Invinite-Delivery); dedupe on it

created_at.description: When the event happened; deliveries are NOT ordered — order by this and the event phase

ws.summary: WebSocket filings stream and live earnings-call transcripts
ws.description:
Upgrade to a WebSocket connection to receive real-time SEC filing events. Authenticate with API Key. WebSocket sessions are unmetered: they cost no credits (hence no `x-credits`).

Live earnings-call transcripts (channel `earnings-calls.live`, requires the PRO plan; the socket itself needs STANDARD): send a `subscribe` frame with an `event_id` or a `cik` and receive `subscribed`, then `transcript_segment` frames as the call is spoken, `speaker_names` snapshots, the lifecycle frames `call_started` / `call_ended` / `transcript_provisional` / `transcript_ready` / `rescheduled` (after `transcript_ready` or `rescheduled` the subscription ends with `unsubscribed`, whose `reason` names why; it also ends 2 h after `call_ended`, when the call will produce nothing more, or 12 h after the scheduled start). Finals are delivered in `seq` order; a `gap` frame reports a range that did not arrive within 1.5 s (a late final may still follow). To resume after a reconnect, subscribe again with `since_seq` = the last final seq you hold: the missed finals are replayed before live delivery continues (`resume_unavailable` when the call cannot be replayed). An `error` frame (code `unavailable`) reports a server-side failure; the socket always stays open.

Keyword alerts and guidance flashes: a `subscribe` with `keywords` (up to 20; `keyword_match` exact | stem, `speaker_roles` to keep management's words only) also sends a `keyword_hit` frame for every final segment that contains one — with the speaker's provisional name / role, the previous final as context and `latency_ms` (relay time inside the API process minus the segment's own end time; the client's network is excluded). Every subscription of a call receives `guidance_flash` frames: forward-looking numbers extracted seconds after they are spoken. `scope: all_live` with `keywords` (no `event_id` / `cik`; `min_rank` limits the companies; `events` may add `guidance_flash`) follows every call being captured live for one subscription slot and receives keyword hits only, never segments; a `warning` frame (`global_scope_degraded`) says a new call was not attached. At `transcript_ready` an `all_live` subscription also gets the final transcript's hits once (`layer: final`), without those a live hit already covered within ± 5 s.

Live price ticks: `prices: true` on a per-call subscription adds `price_tick` frames (≤ 1/s): the second's OHLC, volume, return in bp since the last trade before the call start and since the previous close, and `call_ms` on the transcript clock. Temporal coincidence, not attribution of cause; pre-market and after-hours bars are sparse. `prices` with `scope: all_live` is refused (`bad_message`); `GET /v1/earnings-calls/live` says `live_prices: true` while ticks flow. Minimum tier for display: FREE.

context_before.description: The previous final / turn of the call (≤ 300 chars); a final is often half a sentence

speaker_name.description: From the live speaker-name snapshot (null while unnamed) or the final transcript

speaker_role.description: executive | ir_host | analyst | operator; null while unnamed

layer.description: live = a live final; final = the final transcript at transcript_ready (once per subscription)

latency_ms.description: live only: relay time inside the API process minus the segment's own end time (excludes the client's network); null when the call's clock is unknown

partial.description: Present (true) only when a detail was still missing 60 s after the event

post.description: A test delivery, or the notice that the subscription was disabled

data.description: A test delivery, or the notice that the subscription was disabled
